newsitem.title: GERMANY: BMW profits up 30 percent in first half.
newsitem.headline: BMW profits up 30 percent in first half.

text.p: Luxury carmaker Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG said Tuesday its profits rose 30 percent in the first half of 1997 as new models and a strong dollar boosted results.

BMW, which reported an 18.5 percent rise in 1996 profits, said its first-half net profit climbed to 435 million marks ($236.9 million) from 335 million marks ($182.5 million) on sales growth of 15.5 percent to 29.1 billion marks ($15.8 billion).
The carmaker, which is known for offering conservative forecasts, added it expected sales and profit to climb for the year as a whole but did not specify by how much.
Analysts said the results reflected the strength of the dollar as much as the undeniable success of new models like the 5-Series executive class sedan and the Z3 sports car.

"The figures are a bit better than expected, but generally in line with our forecasts," said Stephen Reitman, analyst at Merrill Lynch in London. "We should see profits up by about one third for the year as a whole."
Deliveries of BMW-branded cars climbed to 350,788 vehicles from 318,625. Deliveries of cars made by Britain's Rover Group, which BMW bought in 1994, climbed to 250,382 vehicles from 238,154.

Analysts said the first-half figures reinforced their belief that BMW will report group net profit of around one billion marks ($545 million) for the year as a whole -- compared with 820 million ($468 million) in 1996.

Although BMW-branded cars made a strong advance in the United States, where deliveries climbed 25 percent to 62,000 units, the most statisfying story for the first half may have been BMW's success in its home market.
BMW, which faces a tough battle with Audi AG, said its share of the German car market climbed to 6.5 percent in the first half from 6.1 percent in first half 1996.

With the 5-Series giving it an edge in the market share battle, BMW has kept demand for its long-serving 3-Series alive with no fewer than eight variations, including compact, cabriolet and station wagon versions, one analyst said.
